newsitem.title: CANADA: Placer near deal on Marcopper divestiture.
newsitem.headline: Placer near deal on Marcopper divestiture.

text.p: Placer Dome Inc said Wednesday it was nearing an agreement to divest its 40 percent stake in the Marcopper mine in the Philippines to the mine's majority owner.
"There's been a lot of negotiating going on recently. I'd say we're close to reaching an agreement," chief executive John Willson said in an interview.

Placer announced last month that it would seek to transfer ownership of its stake in Marcopper Mining Corp to the Philippine majority owner. The copper mine suffered a major leak of tailings in March.

The mine has been closed since then and efforts are underway to permanently plug the leak. Placer wrote off its investment in Marcopper earlier this year and took a US$43 million charge to earnings for the accident. Two Placer executives at Marcopper face criminal charges.
Willson said Placer is working with non-governmental organizations on a plan to compensate local residents who suffered as a result of the accident.
He said Placer may have taken a bigger charge than will ultimately prove necessary to cover the costs.

"We may have overcharged ourselves but I don't think we'll...get money back," he said. "If we had overcharged ourselves for that, then we would write it back. But we don't expect there to be a great difference."

Willson reiterated that Placer is interested in Bre-X Minerals Ltd, which controls the giant Busang gold deposit in Indonesia. But he declined to comment on rumors that Placer might make a bid for Bre-X, potentially in partnership with another major mining company. Willson repeated that Placer prefers projects that result from its own exploration efforts, but it will look at attractive acquisitions.
